small_guidance:
- Add larger-tile autotune configs targeted at this square 2048×8192×8192 GEMM: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8 num_stages=4, and BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=5; also try GROUP_M=4 since M=2048 only has 8-16 row tiles.
- Drop the `eviction_policy="evict_last"` on the weight load — weights are streamed once across K and never reused within a program, so default policy is better; also remove tail masking on x/w loads since M, N, K are all multiples of 128 (use `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on offs to enable wider vector loads).
- Cast `acc` to fp16/bf16 only at store-time isn't applicable (output is fp32), but you can convert the bias load to fp32 explicitly and apply scaling+hardtanh+GELU fused exactly as now — keep epilogue but consider using `tl.fdiv` style tanh-approx GELU (slightly cheaper than erf) since the hardtanh-clamped input is bounded.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a split-K or stream-K persistent GEMM: with M=2048, N=8192, K=8192 the grid is only 16×64=1024 tiles, modest for a 4090; a persistent kernel with one program per SM looping over assigned tiles will reduce launch/scheduling overhead and improve L2 reuse of the heavy 256MB weight matrix.
- Avoid materializing the transposed weight (`wt = W.t().contiguous()`) — it doubles weight memory traffic and adds a one-time 256MB copy per forward when cache misses. Instead, load W in its native (N, K) layout with a (BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) tile via `tl.load` and use `tl.dot(x, w_tile.trans())` or load with swapped strides directly into the K-inner accumulator, removing the transpose entirely.
- Consider an fp16/bf16 compute path: cast x and W to bf16 on the fly inside the kernel (or pre-cache W as bf16) and accumulate in fp32 with `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` replaced by bf16 inputs — this roughly doubles tensor-core throughput on Ada and is the main lever to get past 2× speedup on a compute-bound 8192³ GEMM.
